curated-gf-baloo-thambi-2-gf-syne-mono: Syne Mono keeps every character in a constant-width slot, with a sizable lowercase and gaps that stay wide, handy for something like a commit graph visual. Baloo Thambi 2 up top is the chatty one, and the monospace body wears out over long paragraphs.
curated-gf-barriecito-fs-public-sans: Public Sans reads sturdy and trustworthy, its hefty lowercase opening broad on every curve, fine even on a landscaping truck decal. Barriecito is the showoff with its tipped-ladle bowls, and Public Sans is the one that does the steady talking.
curated-gf-barrio-gf-bhutuka-expanded-on: BhuTuka Expanded One walks rather than runs, with curvy, unclamped letters and a literary feel. Barrio's nearly shut c terminals up top make a tight, commanding opening, and the open body letters then loosen things up for brief copy.
curated-gf-battambang-gf-gidole: Battambang squeezes its ascenders short and leaves every curve open like a jaw. Gidole follows with a high midline and terminals held apart like scissor blades, and its neon-tube consistency in every stroke is what the pair does best.
curated-gf-battambang-gf-noticia-text: Battambang has short ascenders and curves that gape open at every turn. Noticia Text sits next to it feeling dignified and bookish, its lowercase filling most of the letter height and its big entrance strokes giving the two a pleasing tension.
curated-gf-battambang-gf-odor-mean-chey: Odor Mean Chey has tall, rounded lowercase with a, e and s squeezed to narrow mouths, fit for a short film title card. Battambang's open jaws and compressed ascenders sit against that tightness, and that open-versus-closed tension is the pair's best quality.
curated-gf-baumans-gf-cantarell: Commanding and a bit cheeky, Baumans swings its c like a wrench opened wide, say, for a kids school lunch label. And Cantarell, approachable beneath it, pulls its c tips well apart and lets its arches match the stems.
curated-gf-bayon-fs-erode: Erode reads with a tall middle band, shallow ascenders and a gentle ebb and flow of stroke weight. Bayon's fused, stencil-like glyphs have no hairlines at all, and that hard line against the mellow body range is what stands out.
curated-gf-bellota-gf-nata-sans: Bellota hangs the ends of its s far from the spine, every stroke traced as if with one stylus. It leads with that commanding quirk while Nata Sans does the quieter work, a large central band and wide, unclosed curves.
curated-gf-benne-gf-victor-mono: Victor Mono leaves its bowls unfinished on one side and spaces its glyphs loosely, which suits an api reference. Benne's snug fit and worn-stamp thick-thin play do the dignified work, and Victor Mono handles the precise, structured part.
